name: Arameans
also_known_as: Syrians (the KJV's usual translation of Aram)
summary: A Semitic people of Syria and upper Mesopotamia, closely related to Israel's own ancestors — 'A Syrian ready to perish was my father'. Their kingdom at Damascus was Israel's great northern rival in the days of Elijah and Elisha. Their language, Aramaic, became the common tongue of the Near East. Parts of Ezra and Daniel are written in it, and Jesus spoke it.
name_meaning: Aram, possibly 'highland'. The KJV follows the Greek Septuagint in translating Aram as 'Syria'.

origin.account: Aram was the fifth son of Shem. A second Aram appears as grandson of Nahor, Abraham's brother. Abraham's relatives in Haran — Bethuel, Laban, Rebekah, Rachel and Leah — are all called Syrians (Arameans). Historically the Arameans appear in Assyrian records from about 1100 BC, spreading across Syria and Mesopotamia and founding city-states such as Damascus, Zobah, Hamath and Bit-Adini.

lineage.notes: Israel's closest relatives outside Abraham's own descendants. Isaac and Jacob both married Aramean women from Padan-aram, so Israel's twelve tribal fathers had Aramean mothers. Moses told each Israelite to confess at the altar, 'A Syrian ready to perish was my father'.

homeland.region: Aram — Syria and the upper Euphrates (Aram-Naharaim)
homeland.description: From the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon mountains eastward across the Syrian steppe to the Euphrates and the Habur. The Damascus oasis, watered by the Abana and Pharpar rivers, was the heart of the southern Aramean kingdom. 'Padan-aram', the plain of Aram around Haran, was the family homeland of the patriarchs.
homeland.modern_location: Syria, south-eastern Turkey, northern Iraq and parts of Lebanon.

places.name: Damascus
places.note: Capital of Aram; where Saul of Tarsus was converted.

places.name: Haran / Padan-aram
places.note: Home of Laban and Rebekah's family.

places.name: Rivers Abana and Pharpar
places.note: Naaman's pride: 'Are not Abana and Pharpar… better than all the waters of Israel?'

places.name: Zobah
places.note: Kingdom of Hadadezer, defeated by David.

places.name: Tel Dan
places.note: Where an Aramean king's victory stele mentioning the 'house of David' was found.

timeline.event: Abraham's servant finds Rebekah among Nahor's family in Aram-Naharaim.
Jacob serves 'Laban the Syrian' twenty years; they part with a covenant heap named in both Aramaic (Jegar-sahadutha) and Hebrew (Galeed).
Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia (Aram-Naharaim) oppresses Israel; Othniel delivers them.
David defeats Hadadezer of Zobah and the Syrians of Damascus and puts garrisons in Damascus.
Ben-hadad besieges Samaria. Elijah is told to anoint Hazael, Naaman is healed through Elisha, and the Syrian army is struck blind at Dothan.
Hazael murders Ben-hadad, becomes king, and brutally oppresses Israel, as Elisha wept to foresee.
Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel attack Ahaz. Isaiah gives the sign of Immanuel.
Tiglath-pileser III takes Damascus, deports its people to Kir and kills Rezin.
Aramaic is the empire's official language; letters in Ezra 4–7 and Daniel 2:4–7:28 are written in it.
Saul is converted on the Damascus road and preaches in the synagogues of Damascus.

religion.practices: Naaman, after his healing, asked pardon for bowing in the house of Rimmon beside his master. The Syrians thought Israel's God was 'God of the hills' but not the valleys and were defeated to prove otherwise. Ahaz copied a Damascus altar for the Temple.

importance: The Arameans are Israel's kin — the family of Rebekah, Rachel and Leah — and for two centuries its most dangerous neighbour. The Syrian wars are the background of Elijah's and Elisha's ministries, including Naaman's healing, which Jesus cites as God's grace to a Gentile. Aramaic, spread by Aramean scribes and merchants, became the everyday language of Jesus and the apostles: 'Talitha cumi', 'Ephphatha', 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani', 'Abba'.

impact.how: Built his family and fortune in Laban's house.

impact.who: Naaman and the little Israelite maid
impact.how: A captive girl's witness led a Syrian general to healing and faith in the one God.
Saw the hills full of fiery horses and chariots around the Syrian army.
Killed by a random arrow at Ramoth-gilead fighting Syria.
Converted near Damascus and baptised by Ananias there.

notable_people.name: Ben-hadad
notable_people.role: Title/name of several kings of Damascus

notable_people.name: Naaman
notable_people.role: Captain of the Syrian host, healed of leprosy

notable_people.name: Hazael
notable_people.role: King of Syria who oppressed Israel

key_verses.text: And thou shalt speak and say before the LORD thy God, A Syrian ready to perish was my father, and he went down into Egypt, and sojourned there with a few, and became there a nation, great, mighty, and populous:

And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.

And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them. And Elisha prayed, and said, LORD, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.
And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.

fate.summary: The Aramean states were annexed by Assyria in the 8th century BC, but Aramaic language and culture outlasted the kingdoms. It was the lingua franca from Egypt to India under the Persians, and in its Syriac form became the language of eastern Christianity.

today.summary: Aramaic is still spoken in several dialects: Western Neo-Aramaic in Maaloula, Syria, and Eastern dialects among Assyrian, Chaldean and Syriac Christians and some Jewish and Mandaean communities. Syriac Christians of the Syriac Orthodox and other churches often identify as Arameans. In September 2014 Israel became the first country to recognise 'Aramean' as a nationality.
today.descendants: Aramaic-speaking and Syriac Christian communities of Syria, Iraq, Turkey, Lebanon, Israel and the diaspora.
today.modern_legacy: Aramaic words in the Gospels; the Syriac Peshitta Bible; the 'square' script of modern Hebrew, which descends from the Aramaic alphabet.

archaeology.name: Tel Dan Stele
archaeology.significance: An Aramean king (probably Hazael) claims to have killed the king of Israel and the king of the 'house of David'.

archaeology.significance: Objects inscribed as belonging to 'our lord Hazael'.
